design_question: Separation-logic ownership contracts (owned(p)-style pre/postconditions) can be monitored at run time by a per-byte ownership map with transfer on call/return. Which fragment of the contract language has a computational interpretation such that an accepted run really satisfied every contract as a separation-logic assertion, when is the monitor complete, and what does it assume about unannotated code?

tier_justification: Consequence of identifying frames by call depth (as Fulminate's ghost state does) when leaks are not checked. Recorded search (2026-11-20): web searches for runtime checking of separation logic with ownership monitors, completeness, precise assertions, disjunction, online footprint choice and backtracking, gradual verification, and mechanized separation algebras; reading of Fulminate (full text), Nguyen-Kuncak-Chin (full text), O'Hearn-Yang-Reynolds (full text), compiler-team #942 (full text) and the Miri prototype source. No source examined states this result in this form or mechanizes it; the ideas are standard, hence T1 rather than T3.
plain_claim: Without the leak check, in this depth-indexed monitor a byte leaked by one callee stays attributed to depth 1, and a later sibling callee at depth 1 that was given only owned 1 reads the leaked byte 0 and is accepted, although that call does not satisfy its contract even on its own.
nonvacuity_witness: Closed statement about a concrete instance; it has no hypotheses and is its own witness.
non_claims: Specific to depth-indexed attribution without a leak check. Three return policies should be distinguished: (i) exact postconditions with a leak check (this model; required for the exact Satisfies); (ii) affine postconditions, where unmentioned callee resources may be discarded and are then inaccessible to everyone (as in affine separation logic, e.g. the \GC predicate of Separation Logic Foundations); (iii) the examined Miri prototype, which on frame pop inserts every remaining entry of the callee frame into the caller frame - the caller then holds ownership the postcondition did not state. Policies (ii) and (iii) are not modeled.
Not examined whether any implementation exhibits this.

Toy model only: straight-line programs (no branching, loops, recursion, allocation, deallocation, concurrency), one address per byte, contracts without logical variables, value-binding resource outputs (CN's take, the let-bound results of owned in compiler-team #942), function parameters or return values, existentials, recursive predicates or iterated separating conjunction; ownership is whole (no fractional or read-only permissions) and there are no allocation-block tokens (alloc_block). Nothing is claimed about Fulminate, CN, Miri or any implementation (any such connection is a separate modeling-bridge claim).
prior_art: Rini Banerjee, Kayvan Memarian, Dhruv Makwana, Christopher Pulte, Neel Krishnaswami, Peter Sewell, 'Fulminate: Testing CN Separation-Logic Specifications in C', Proc. ACM Program. Lang. 9(POPL), Article 43, 2025, doi:10.1145/3704879. Sec. 2.3: reified ghost state records the C stack depth owning each byte; at a call the precondition's resources must be mapped at the caller's depth and are moved to the current depth, postconditions move them back, and leak checking is optional; Sec. 4.5.3: memory accesses are (optionally) instrumented to check ownership at the current depth. Sec. 2.4.2: CN restricts classical separation logic (resource outputs computed from inputs; if-then-else with guarded clauses instead of general disjunction, 'similar to RefinedC') so that runtime checking can determine 'without backtracking' which clause applies. Sec. 3.4: Theorem 3.5 and Corollary 3.6 relate two dynamic semantics (resource passing and the ghost-state instrumentation: they bisimulate and fail under the same conditions); they do not relate a monitor to a declarative satisfaction relation. Sec. 4.6: generated code is placed in a single file and multiple-file compilation units are not handled at present; the paper does not discuss uninstrumented or unannotated callees.

Christopher Pulte, Dhruv C. Makwana, Thomas Sewell, Kayvan Memarian, Peter Sewell, Neel Krishnaswami, 'CN: Verifying Systems C Code with Separation-Logic Refinement Types', Proc. ACM Program. Lang. 7(POPL), Article 1, 2023, doi:10.1145/3571194. Introduces CN, a separation-logic refinement type system for C (static verification); Fulminate tests specifications written in CN's specification language at run time. CN restricts specifications so that resources and logical variables can be inferred without backtracking: 'CN does not allow general disjunction in predicate definitions; instead predicate definitions are ordered lists of guarded cases' (Sec. 2.9); resource types use 'a conditional rather than a traditional disjunction to avoid backtracking during typechecking' (Sec. 4.1); and logical variables may be introduced only as outputs of resources, through resource-let-bindings such as let O = Owned<struct s>(p), because unrestricted quantifiers would allow imprecise specifications (Sec. 2.6, 2.12). Sec. 6 says this well-moded style of assertion 'should also be amenable to runtime checking (though we leave this to future work)'. The paper defines no runtime monitor.

Prototype ownership tracking in Miri: repository JoJoDeveloping/miri, branch 'fulminate', commit a33a3c076f10bd42c742ca9eec9c30ed1d0166af (author Johannes Hostert, 2025-08-18; src/ownership/mod.rs, src/ownership/fraction.rs). One map per annotated frame from bytes (and allocation block tokens) to dyadic fractions; writes require the full fraction, reads a nonzero one; owned transfers a full fraction between the top annotated frame and its parent (into the child in preconditions, into the parent in postconditions; the partial-split variant is marked #[allow(unused)]); source comment: 'If non-ownership-annotated funcs are called, we treat it as if they were inlined', i.e. they run in the topmost annotated frame with access checks still active; when an annotated frame is popped (on_stack_pop) every remaining entry is inserted into the parent frame (no check that the popped frame is empty is made there). compiler-team #942 links this prototype directly: its section 'Fulminate' states that Johannes Hostert 'has already implemented a prototype runtime ownership tracker in Miri' and links https://github.com/JoJoDeveloping/miri/tree/fulminate, and its sections 'Examples', 'Semantics of owned and alloc_block' and 'Miri implementation' link example_dream.rs at commit a33a3c076f10bd42c742ca9eec9c30ed1d0166af (in 'Miri implementation' as a 'prototype ownership checker for contracts in Miri'; in 'Examples' at line 155). That commit was the head of branch 'fulminate' when checked (2026-11-20), so the source summarized here is the revision #942 links; #942 links example_dream.rs, not src/ownership/ itself, and none of the comments on #942 links the prototype.

Arthur Chargueraud, 'Separation Logic Foundations', Software Foundations Vol. 6 (Coq), https://softwarefoundations.cis.upenn.edu - mechanized separation logic whose 'Affine' chapter generalizes the linear (exact) logic so that heap predicates may be discarded (the \GC predicate), as needed for garbage-collected languages; this is the affine alternative to the exact postconditions enforced here by the leak check.
